The register contrast occurs only with vowels of the main syllable.' -- verbatim as quoted, at the stated locator (p.63, after the vowel-inventory paragra…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Hrê words are sesquisyllabic: at most an unstressed presyllable followed by the main syllable, which is word-final and always carries the stress; monosyllables are stressed main syllables. Equivalent to fixed word-final stress. Independently confirmed by Trebilco, Trebilco & Đinh Nghĩa 1974: ix ('In two syllable words the second syllable is always accented. The first syllable is almost never accented'; 'There are no tones in Hrê', p. viii) and, at family level, Smith 1972: 1.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned in any source; presyllable described as unstressed.
new_statements.exceptions: Phillips gives none. Trebilco et al. 1974 hedge slightly ('the first syllable is almost never accented') and note 'very few three syllable words' without stating their stress; no lexical exceptions listed. Register (tense vs lax/breathy) contrast is confined to the main-syllable vowel; no tone.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement about citation-form word shape (presyllable + main syllable); nothing said about phrase-level prominence. Phillips describes the Minh-Long district dialect (Quảng Ngãi); Trebilco et al. base theirs on Batơ, Gia-Vụt, Minh-Long and An-Lão.
new_statements.identity_note: Phillips 1973 describes the Minh-Long district dialect of Hrê (Quảng Ngãi); his footnote notes the Sơn-Hà dialect has a somewhat different vowel inventory but says nothing different about stress. Trebilco et al. 1974 is based on Batơ, Gia-Vụt, Minh-Long and An-Lão speech. All are Hre proper, glottocode hree1244 (ISO hre); Glottolog lists no sub-dialect codes.
